_: Hand-established ground truth for correspondence, figma section 17 -> web section 18 (the footer). Scored by the user 2026-08-12. THIS PAIR IS THE HELD-OUT VALIDATION: the xAlignment change in anchors.js was derived from f12-w13 and f14-w15, so this is the only scored pair not contaminated by having seen the answers.
_truth: Keyed by the figma element's orderIndex. A number is the matching web orderIndex; 'missing' = designed but not built; 'decor' = design-only decoration; '?' = undecidable, excluded from scoring.
_webExtra: Web 17-68 - the entire link-column area and the bottom certification bar. Fifty-two elements with no counterpart in the audited Figma frame, because the design's footer frame covers ONLY the purple contact band (655px against the page's 916px). The file has a page named '----Header/Navigation & Footer for Dev---', so these are almost certainly designed elsewhere; within the scope of a single-frame audit they are correctly 'extra'. This is a frame-scoping artifact, not a defect, and it is the whole reason this pair's ratio is 2.88.
_note: 17 real matches, 7 excluded as '?' (the section container and the six small location/phone glyphs inside the address cards). No 'missing' and no 'decor'. The layouts differ structurally in X: the design stacks heading above cards (heading x=220 y=100, cards x=221/714/1207 at y=258) while the page puts them side by side (heading x=192 y=48, cards x=582/972/1362 at y=48). Card widths differ too - 493 designed against 366 built. That makes this the hardest available test of x-based anchoring, since x agreement is the signal the matcher trusts most.
